Ellen: quick report from the int8 onboarding run: intermittent funcall parse failures under burst load
Ravi: short example?
Ellen: proxy log snippet:
```nRECV 2026-03-22T22:40:00Z id=run42 body="{\"tool\":\"fetch\",\"args\":[{\"k\":\"x\"}]"
SEND 2026-03-22T22:40:00Z id=run42 tail="..."
ERROR parse id=run42 Reason=unterminated_array
```
Tom: pattern? only under high concurrency?
Ellen: yes. repro: concurrency 80, sustained 500 qps for 5m -> ~0.4% malformed. Lower concurrency -> drops to 0.01%
Ravi: could be chunk coalescing or buffer reuse in PTQ runtime. Did you try disabling zero-copy flush?
Ellen: tried `--no-zero-copy` and `--flush-interval=5ms` -> errors drop to 0.03% but not zero
Tom: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) sentinel token appended server-side (e.g. "__TOOL_END__"), 2) UTF-8 validation at serialization boundary, 3) return 5xx on partial stream so client retries
qa-bot: canary config applied: max_parallel=25 by ci/canary at 2026-03-22T22:38
Ravi: i can instrument serializer to check last 4 bytes are a closing bracket and valid utf8; if not, abort with 502 and telemetry raw_tail_hex
Ellen: telemetry dims: model, quant_mode, canary_parallel, raw_tail_prefix_b64
Tom: also add client-side parse retry with jitter for canary runs; that buys time while runtime fix lands
Ellen: i'll open quicknote with repro script and sample tails, and create PR request for the serializer guard
Ravi: i'll prototype sentinel append in runtime and a small benchmark to measure extra latency
Tom: good. if error rate rises above 1% for 10m, page @eng-runtime and @infra
Ellen: thanks team, catching this in canary saved us from noisy downstream errors
